title: A Cat Is A Cat (Not A Dog!): Unraveling Information Mix-ups in Text-to-Image Encoders through Causal Analysis and Embedding Optimization
role: The text-encoder candidate: says the CLIP causal mask copies the first subject into the second token, and fixes it by optimizing the prompt embedding with no boxes
enters: a combination: text encoder (causal self-attention mask), showing up as overlapping cross-attention maps
enters_evidence: measurement on 400 two-animal prompts, SD1.4: order swap flips which animal appears alone (46.00% vs 20.00%, swapped 21.75% vs 47.00%); masking animal tokens leaves them drawn from special tokens; token-map link argued
changes: optimizes each object token's text embedding once before sampling: closer to its embedding from 'a photo of a <obj>', further from other tokens (cosine loss, at most 20 iterations)
training: nothing trained; no boxes, masks or LLM; needs object token positions and one extra text-encoder call per object
model: SD1.4 (CLIP ViT-L/14, PNDM, 50 steps, CFG 7.5) for all main results; supplement adds SD1.5+ELLA, SDXL-Turbo, SD3 on T2I-CompBench colour set
similar_subjects: 400 prompts over 17 animals, SD1.4, OWL-ViT boxes overlapping >90% = fused: only-fused 9.5% -> 8.5%, both present 14.5% -> 15.0%, info bias 2.65 -> 1.39 (1 = balanced); on Attend-and-Excite only-fused 11.5% -> 7.5%; mixed-category spatial set only-fused 0.2%
which_pairs: single-word CLIP cosine 0.24 (panda-mouse) to 0.60 (frog-turtle); text says similar embeddings give overlapping cross-attention maps and mixture; first-named subject dominates; no per-pair leakage rate against similarity
when: not measured; map distances taken 'in the early denoising steps' without naming them
cost: no extra UNet passes; 8.21 s/image SD1.4 vs 9.14 s/image with TEBOpt on one RTX 3090
headline: info bias (only-first / only-second, 1 = balanced) 2.65 -> 1.39 on SD1.4 over 400 two-animal prompts, reported as a 125.42% balance improvement (164.71% - 39.29% distance from balance)
suggests: (inferred) compute text cosine both for names alone and for the two tokens inside CO3's joint prompt on both SDXL encoders; TEBOpt could run in front of CO3 with no boxes but its metric cannot see part-borrowing between two separate bodies
